external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store whose own identity provider vouches for them to the broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify which franchise colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies colleague and group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise colleagues' own identity provider that vouches for them to the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, supplies public signing-key material, receives HR changes, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: Tokens are valid for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before expiry. The text does not state the broker's authentication mechanism, transport, interface type, or exposure.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses the token's groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: The store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state whether the key store is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state whether the directory is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: The log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not state whether the log is encrypted at rest.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the identity broker using a vouch from the franchise identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.data_description: Vouch for a franchise colleague's sign-in

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and group list.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the token to the store admin console and uses authorized functions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.data_description: Token and price or transaction administration requests

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads the signing key from the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls colleague and group-membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The broker also uses this update to stop leavers being colleagues.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains its directory of colleagues and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home from which they can sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

assumptions.assumption: The key store contains confidential data because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key; signing keys are secrets.

assumptions.assumption: The directory contains confidential data because it holds colleague identities and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in; colleague identity information is personal data.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log contains confidential data because it records sign-ins that identify colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log; sign-in records identify people.
